This is a terrific law that is widely misunderstood by Americans.

It's really about who owns information, ie your personal data. Think of the concept of publishing rights - who owns the right to publish details of your life - you, or Google? Because Google is making a fuckton of money off of publishing that information.

There's no censorship here - this is merely regulation of the search engine space. Truthfully I've yet to find any cases where censorship is relevant - that bullshit DailyMail article notwithstanding. Further, consider that Google is the party being regulated and this could/will impact their profits and ability to do whatever they want (a cherished corporate freedom in the USA!). Therefore Google has the incentive to execute their enforcement of this law purposely in such a way as to generate negative press, ie they're trying their damndest to generate public anger and push-back so the law can be amended.

Google, unfortunately for them, is too American in their thinking and has zero chance of repealing this legislation, especially in France.
